body.heading: Collect the rainbow
paragraphs: Hunt for fallen petals and leaves in as many colours as you can find — red, orange, yellow, green, purple, pink, white, and brown.
Only take what has already fallen. Fallen petals are the garden's gifts; flowers still growing are gifts for bees and everyone else.

body.heading: Build the wheel
paragraphs: Arrange your finds in a big circle on the paper, in rainbow order. Each colour melts into the next, like a wheel of paint.
Step back and look. A garden holds the whole rainbow at once, if you gather it gently.

body.heading: Name the shades
paragraphs: Look closely at one colour family. How many different greens did you find? Light green, dark green, yellow-green, blue-green.
Artists mix paints to get these shades. The garden grows them all for free.

takeaway: Fallen petals and leaves can build a whole rainbow wheel, showing every colour the garden grows.
safetyNotes: Only collect petals and leaves that have already fallen. Never pick flowers from gardens without the owner's permission, and wash your hands afterwards.
screenFreeExtension: Take a photo of your wheel, then return everything to the garden so it can feed the soil.
